scope: Representative classical and selected later biological model families for a numerical-method atlas. All entries are survey-only; no biological simulation or validation is added by this survey.

models.name: Logistic population growth
models.meaning: Density-limited growth with carrying capacity K. It is the simplest biological ODE baseline.
models.numerics: Positivity, preservation of equilibria and overshoot of K; an accurate-looking curve can still violate the invariant interval.
models.verification: Compare with N(t)=K/[1+(K/N0−1)exp(−rt)] for N0>0; measure temporal order and behavior near 0 and K.
models.scope: The linked original is the later 1847 memoir; the 1838 note itself was not audited. The differential equation is not the discrete logistic map.

models.name: Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics
models.meaning: Enzyme saturation; the full mass-action system resolves the transient complex C, while the rate law eliminates a fast variable.
models.numerics: Fast initial layers and stiffness; full and reduced models have different validity regimes. Under the usual quasi-steady approximation KM=(k−1+k2)/k1.
models.verification: Check E+C and S+C+P conservation in the closed mechanism. Compare reduced and full systems as enzyme/substrate scales vary, rather than calling the reduction exact.
models.scope: The 1913 rapid-equilibrium interpretation and the 1925 quasi-steady-state derivation must remain distinct.

models.name: Lotka–Volterra predator–prey
models.equation: \dot x=\alpha x-\beta xy,\qquad\dot y=\delta xy-\gamma y.
models.meaning: Coupled prey growth and predation; a phase-plane and long-time integration test.
models.numerics: Positive states and artificial damping or growth of closed orbits. Periodic orbits of this idealized system are not attracting limit cycles.
models.verification: Monitor H=δx−γ ln(x)+βy−α ln(y) for positive x,y, and compare orbit drift under step refinement.

models.name: McKendrick age-structured population
models.meaning: Individuals move through age a at unit speed; newborns enter through a nonlocal renewal boundary.
models.numerics: Upwind/FV transport in age, birth-boundary quadrature and truncation of the infinite age interval.
models.verification: Use characteristic survival along cohorts and check d∫n da/dt=births−deaths, including any artificial oldest-age outflow.
models.scope: This is the classical age-transport form; the later von Foerster lineage is acknowledged without treating its date as the first appearance.

models.name: SIR and SEIR compartment models
models.equation: \dot s=-\beta si,\quad\dot i=\beta si-\gamma i,\quad\dot r=\gamma i,\quad s+i+r=1.
models.meaning: Closed, well-mixed normalized population fractions. SEIR adds an exposed compartment and a progression rate.
models.numerics: Nonnegative compartments, invariant total population and correct resolution of epidemic peak times.
models.verification: Check total 1 and i+s−(γ/β)ln(s) for β>0,s>0; compare early growth rate βs0−γ and final-size relation in the closed SIR specialization.
models.scope: The original general epidemic framework is broader than this SIR specialization. Population-count and fraction conventions give different β definitions.

models.name: Fisher–KPP invasion front
models.meaning: Spatial spread of an invading population or advantageous allele, represented by a reaction–diffusion front.
models.numerics: Spatial and temporal front-speed errors; leading-edge resolution, positivity and finite-domain boundary contamination.
models.verification: Use the Ablowitz–Zeppetella exact front at c=5√(Dr/6), or test the minimal speed 2√(Dr) only with the appropriate steep initial-data regime on a sufficiently large domain.
models.scope: Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original remains an archival follow-up. The exact special speed is not the minimal speed.

models.name: Monod growth and chemostat
models.meaning: Nutrient-limited biomass X, substrate S, yield Y and chemostat dilution d; d=0 gives a closed batch model.
models.numerics: Washout near a threshold, disparate resource/growth scales, positivity and the distinction between yield and rate constants.
models.verification: For d=0 check S+X/Y. For d>0 use d(S+X/Y)/dt=d[Sin−(S+X/Y)] and verify the washout equilibrium.
models.scope: This writes one constant-yield extension of saturation growth, not a universal metabolic model.

models.name: Hodgkin–Huxley membrane dynamics
models.meaning: Voltage and gating variables z=m,h,n describe an ionic excitable membrane. A cable extension adds spatial axial current.
models.numerics: Stiff gates, removable singularities in rate formulas, gating bounds, voltage/current sign and temperature conventions.
models.verification: Select an explicitly versioned CellML/reference convention, verify resting equilibrium and gate relaxation at clamped voltage, then refine spike time and waveform.
models.scope: The original squid-axon model is not a calibrated human cardiac model. No single rate parameter set is selected by this survey.

models.name: Turing reaction–diffusion framework
models.meaning: A framework for diffusion-driven pattern onset around a homogeneous reaction equilibrium, not a unique choice of f and g.
models.numerics: Physical versus numerical instability, domain eigenmodes and errors in the discrete Laplacian dispersion relation.
models.verification: For a selected kinetic law compare eigenvalues of J−k²diag(Du,Dv) with early-time Fourier-mode growth. Show that the k=0 reaction equilibrium is stable before asserting diffusion-driven instability.
models.scope: A spot image or unequal diffusion coefficients alone do not establish a Turing mechanism. Boundary conditions determine the available modes.

models.name: FitzHugh–Nagumo excitation and recovery
models.meaning: A normalized fast excitation/slow recovery model for pulses, refractoriness and spiral waves when extended in space.
models.numerics: Stiff time-scale separation, splitting error, wave-speed convergence and numerical wave breakup.
models.verification: Check ODE fixed points/nullclines and small-perturbation eigenvalues first; then refine a 1D pulse before a 2D spiral movie.
models.scope: This is a common normalized variant; cubic coefficients, recovery signs and nondimensionalization differ between formulations.

models.name: Keller–Segel chemotaxis
models.equation: n_t=D_n\Delta n-\chi\nabla\cdot(n\nabla c),\qquad\tau_c c_t=D_c\Delta c+\alpha n-\lambda c.
models.meaning: Cell density n drifts up a chemoattractant gradient; τc=0 gives an elliptic chemical subproblem.
models.numerics: Cross-coupled flux, positivity, mass conservation and concentrated peaks; spurious undershoots must not be mistaken for physical aggregation or blowup.
models.verification: With zero total cell flux check ∫n conservation, homogeneous equilibria and linear growth; refine the peak and domain before discussing singularity. Use manufactured smooth solutions before aggregation cases.
models.scope: This is a common two-field reduction of a more detailed original formulation. Blowup thresholds depend on dimension, domain, boundary and chemical dynamics.

models.name: Gierer–Meinhardt activator–inhibitor
models.equation: a_t=D_a\Delta a+\rho a^2/h-\mu a+\sigma_a,\qquad h_t=D_h\Delta h+\rho_h a^2-\nu h.
models.meaning: A representative simplified short-range activation/long-range inhibition model.
models.numerics: The inhibitor denominator can become singular; positive h, narrow peaks and reaction stiffness require explicit treatment.
models.verification: Choose a positive homogeneous equilibrium, check its dispersion relation and inhibitor positivity, then refine spike width and pattern wavelength.
models.scope: Source densities, saturation and baseline production vary across the model family. This simplified formula is not a verbatim transcription of every original variant.

models.equation:

abla\cdot oldsymbol u=0,\quad oldsymbol X_t= oldsymbol u( oldsymbol X,t).
models.meaning: Fluid coupled to a deformable structure; biological examples include valves and membranes, once a force/constitutive law is supplied.
models.numerics: Stiff elastic forces, pressure projection, Eulerian–Lagrangian interpolation/spreading and volume leakage.
models.verification: Specify elastic energy and force before solving. Check force transfer, adjoint interpolation/spreading, fluid divergence and enclosed-volume drift on a simple relaxing boundary.
models.scope: Immersed boundary is a numerical coupling method, not itself a closed biological constitutive equation. The existing periodic MAC solver does not implement this coupling.

models.name: Chemical master equation and Gillespie SSA
models.equation: \partial_t P(\boldsymbol n,t)=\sum_j\left[a_j(\boldsymbol n-\boldsymbol\nu_j)P(\boldsymbol n-\boldsymbol\nu_j,t)-a_j(\boldsymbol n)P(\boldsymbol n,t)\right].
models.meaning: Integer molecule counts, reaction jumps νj and propensities aj; SSA samples paths of this continuous-time Markov model.
models.numerics: Correct combinatorial propensities, event ordering, absorbing states and statistical error; tau-leaping is a separate approximation.
models.verification: Use immigration–death reactions ∅→X at constant rate k and X→∅ at rate γn: stationary counts are Poisson(k/γ). Compare ensemble mean, variance and distribution with confidence intervals.
models.scope: The 1977 paper is a foundational SSA reference, not a priority claim for all master equations. SSA is a solver; the reaction network is the model. A seed documents a trajectory, not an ensemble validation.

models.name: Mackey–Glass delayed physiological feedback
models.meaning: Delayed feedback in a normalized physiological control model; delay can change stability and oscillatory behavior.
models.numerics: A history function over [−τ,0], delayed interpolation, propagated derivative discontinuities and delay-aware adaptive stepping.
models.verification: Check the τ=0 ODE limit, a constant equilibrium history and a manufactured forced solution. Compare long-time statistics rather than expecting chaotic trajectories to match pointwise indefinitely.
models.scope: A scalar initial value alone is insufficient. The delayed ODE is distinct from a spatial reaction–diffusion model.

models.name: Replicator evolutionary game dynamics
models.equation: \dot x_i=x_i[(A\boldsymbol x)_i-\boldsymbol x^TA\boldsymbol x],\qquad x_i\geq0,\quad\sum_i x_i=1.
models.meaning: Strategy fractions reproduce according to relative payoff in a specified matrix game.
models.numerics: Preserving the probability simplex, behavior near extinction boundaries, neutral cycles versus attracting equilibria.
models.verification: Check simplex conservation, exact invariant faces and an analytically chosen game equilibrium; use the appropriate game-specific invariant or Lyapunov function.
models.scope: No universal Lyapunov function or equivalence of fixed point and evolutionarily stable strategy is assumed.

models.name: Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion
models.meaning: A simple autocatalytic kinetic law extended in space, useful for reproducible Turing-onset tests.
models.numerics: Reaction stiffness, positive concentrations and the distinction between kinetic Hopf and spatial Turing instabilities.
models.verification: Check u*=a+b, v*=b/(a+b)², then compare mode-growth rates with the linearized discrete and continuum operators under fixed boundaries.
models.scope: A mathematical chemical pattern model; matching a visual biological pattern does not calibrate it to a tissue.

models.name: Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto cross-diffusion
models.meaning: Competition with density-dependent self- and cross-dispersal can produce spatial segregation.
models.numerics: A coupled nonlinear diffusion matrix, loss of simple scalar maximum-principle arguments, positivity and entropy-compatible discretization.
models.verification: Start with manufactured smooth solutions and constant-state equilibria. With reactions removed and no normal flux, conserve each species mass; check coefficient assumptions before claiming an entropy law.
models.scope: The displayed homogeneous-environment reduction omits the original environmental-potential terms. It is not equivalent to two independent scalar diffusion equations.

models.name: Gray–Scott spatial autocatalysis
models.meaning: A chemical feed/decay model whose spatial extension supports diverse spot and wave patterns.
models.numerics: Sensitivity to F,k, diffusion, domain and finite-amplitude initial perturbations; grid-scale patterns and floating-point variation can affect long-time morphology.
models.verification: Record every parameter and the perturbation seed. Verify the homogeneous (1,0) state and early perturbation response, then perform grid/time refinement of quantitative observables.
models.scope: 1983 is the well-mixed CSTR source; Pearson 1993 is the spatial pattern reference. Spot division does not by itself demonstrate cell division or a linear Turing instability.

models.name: Aliev–Panfilov cardiac excitation
models.meaning: A reduced phenomenological excitation/recovery model for cardiac waves and restitution.
models.numerics: Stiff recovery, denominator behavior and sensitivity of wave speed/restitution to resolution and time splitting.
models.verification: Select a specific model encoding and parameters; establish single-cell and 1D conduction convergence before 2D reentry. Compare a restitution curve, not only a spiral image.
models.scope: Monodomain/bidomain tissue models add conductivity tensors and, for bidomain, an extracellular elliptic constraint. They are not automatically included by this two-variable model.

models.name: Repressilator mRNA–protein network
models.meaning: Three repressing genes form a cyclic network; retaining mRNA and protein gives six state variables.
models.numerics: Multiple degradation scales, oscillation onset, phase error and differences between deterministic cycles and noisy individual-cell behavior.
models.verification: Check the symmetric equilibrium and its linear stability. Compare period and amplitude under time refinement after a stated transient.
models.scope: The six-variable form is distinct from a reduced three-protein oscillator; oscillations are parameter-dependent.

models.name: Genetic toggle switch
models.meaning: Mutual repression produces a possible bistable genetic switch in a normalized model.
models.numerics: Parameter-dependent bistability, saddle separatrices, continuation and sensitivity to perturbations near basin boundaries.
models.verification: Find all positive equilibria and their Jacobian eigenvalues; verify hysteresis with sufficiently slow continuation and multiple initial conditions.
models.scope: Bistability is not guaranteed for arbitrary Hill exponents or production rates. Induction, mRNA dynamics and noise are additional model choices.
